ops.title: Flaky on CI: TestAdoptMintedRefusesEveryOffContractHello/control_lane sees PhaseDraining on a freshly-built PhaseReady server
ops.description:
First seen 2026-08-30 on run `33293779860`, job `test (macos-latest)`, step "Test (race, via the process-cap harness)", commit `d9c500a` — a commit that touches ONLY `.github/workflows/fleet-build.yml`, `ci/fleet-refs.txt`, and `scripts/fleet-build.sh`. Nothing in that range can affect `internal/wire`, so this is pre-existing, not a regression.

Verbatim:

    2026/08/30 05:02:59 INFO wire: drain admitted on the frozen preamble peer_pid=25377
    2026/08/30 05:02:59 INFO wire: drain admitted on the frozen preamble peer_pid=25377
    --- FAIL: TestAdoptMintedRefusesEveryOffContractHello (0.00s)
        --- FAIL: TestAdoptMintedRefusesEveryOffContractHello/control_lane (0.00s)
            spawnchannel_internal_test.go:281: AdoptMinted() = wire: server is draining, want a refusal naming "business lane"
    FAIL
    FAIL	github.com/yasyf/daemonkit/internal/wire	7.029s

Every other package in that run passed; `lint` and `swift` in the same run were green.

**Why this is worth more than a flake label.** The subtest builds its own server with `mustServer(t, stubRuntime{phase: PhaseReady}, ...)` and then observes `PhaseDraining`. A freshly-constructed server reporting a phase its runtime never had is state arriving from outside the subtest — a package-level global, or an adjacent subtest's goroutine still writing after its own `t` finished. The two identical `drain admitted on the frozen preamble` lines with the same `peer_pid` immediately before the failure point at the second. If that is right, the same bleed can make an assertion pass for the wrong reason, which is worse than the visible failure.

**Distinct from `6a1314c`**, the fixed-wall-clock Swift deadline family (Deadline/Readiness/SnapshotWatcher). This is the Go side and is not a timing bound — it is a wrong observed value. Both fired on consecutive main pushes on 2026-08-30 (`d9c500a` Go, `b99c8a1` Swift), which is what prompted the triage.

**Reproduction note:** CI runs the suite through `scripts/test.sh`. Never run bare `go test` in this repo — the self-exec suites fork-bomb the machine.</body>

ops.text: Reproduce by running ./scripts/test.sh -race -count=N ./internal/wire/... until the control_lane subtest sees PhaseDraining, or prove it cannot recur

Identify what carries PhaseDraining into a server built by mustServer(t, stubRuntime{phase: PhaseReady}, ...) — shared global, package-level state, or a goroutine from an adjacent subtest still writing
The subtest asserts its own server's phase rather than inheriting whatever an adjacent subtest left behind
